arguments.text: Coins kept in wallets, exchanged for bits through ecommerce. The user, 2026-10-27: "keep the coins in wallets". The tree's coins are its accounting units for work — the time and heat coins the billing door books against a committer and to the author at zero price ("work, not money"), the deposits the hosted gate makes, the coins a shipment line is priced in. Each holder (tenant, agent key, author, the gate) gets a wallet: a Payload record whose balance is the fold of its ledger entries in the docket (Entries by address), never a stored number that could drift; a hook appends each booking, clearing or deposit as a signed entry (ML-DSA-65 through seal) and the wallet's balance is recomputed and verified against bit 0. What coins are not: they are not a cryptocurrency, are not sold, transferred for value or redeemed for money, and carry no claim on anything — keeping them that way keeps them outside securities and crypto-asset regulation. Real payments stay in the payments lead (the tenant's own payment adapter, non-custodial crypto wallets the buyer holds). Measured: holders with a wallet / holders, wallet balances equal to the fold of their entries / wallets (target equal), entries signed and verified / entries. The user, then: "keep the coins in wallets and exchange them for bits". A wallet's coins are spent only for bits the QPU itself serves: compute (a program run at its UUID's address), storage (bytes kept at binding 0 and mirrored by the RAID adapters), and transfer (bytes streamed). The rate is physical, not a price: the heat coin converts by Landauer's bound (erasing one bit costs at least kT ln 2 joules, so a heat coin of E joules at temperature T buys at most E / (kT ln 2) bit operations), and the time coin by the measured throughput of the step that served it (bits per second, from the forecasts). An exchange is one ledger pair, coins debited from the wallet and bits credited to the holder's quota, written by a hook as a double entry that annihilates on reversal; it never runs the other way (bits are not sold back for coins), and coins are never exchanged for money or for another holder's coins. Measured: exchanges whose debit equals the credit at the stated rate / exchanges (target equal), bits served against bits bought per holder, the Landauer ratio (bits bought per joule over 1 / (kT ln 2)) as the efficiency, exact. The user, then: "…to fuse payload ecommerce with the quantum billing". The exchange runs through the ecommerce plugin's own documented mechanisms, not a side ledger: the coin is a currency in the plugin's currencies config (its own code, symbol and decimals, closed-loop: not redeemable for money, not transferable between holders); compute, storage and transfer bits are products whose variants are the bit quantities, priced in coins at the Landauer and throughput rates the billing door computes; a cart is a bit order; the wallet is a custom payment adapter (the plugin's initiatePayment and confirmOrder) that debits the holder's coins by a double entry and refuses when the balance is short; the order's fulfilment is the bits served, booked as the shipment the taken next step already is. So quantum billing (coins earned by work) and ecommerce (bits bought with them) are one flow: billing mints coins into wallets, ecommerce spends them, both in the docket by address. Money products stay priced in real currencies through the tenant's payment adapters (the payments lead), and no product is sold for both. Measured: bit products priced in coins / bit products, orders paid by the wallet adapter whose debit equals the coin price / orders, orders fulfilled (bits served equal to bits bought) / orders paid, exact.

Irrational gateway angles
No next overlaps; every taken step is a shipment in ecommerce

arguments.text: No next overlaps; every taken step is a shipment in ecommerce. The user, 2026-10-27: "no next should overlap as taken steps are tracked as shipments in eccomerce". One next at a time, anywhere: a run takes a lock before its first step (Payload's jobs concurrency key qpu-wave on the app; a lock file by content address under .qpu/ when the app is down) and a second run — a pre-commit next, a CI next, an agent's — waits or refuses with the holder's address; overlapping runs are a typed violation (kind overlap). Measured: runs, overlaps (target 0). Every step a run takes is a shipment in the ecommerce plugin, within its existing collections (addresses, carts, orders, products, transactions, variants; no new collection): the run is an order for its tenant, each step a line of that order whose product is the step and whose variant is its inputs' content address, and the step's completion is the line's fulfilment — shipped (green, its outputs' address as the tracking reference), returned (red, its violation as the reason), or reused (delivered from the sealed record at no cost). The price of a line is the step's measured cost in the billing door's units (time and heat coins), never money taken. A hook writes each shipment as the step ends; the order closes when the run does. Acceptance: steps taken / steps shipped equal, orders closed / runs, overlaps 0 — exact pairs on this page by its hooks. The user, 2026-10-27: "shipping code is a billable trackable task". Shipping code — a commit through the hooks, a merge, a push through pre-push, a deploy, a tagged release — is itself an order line: the product is the act, the variant the shipped content (the commit or artefact address), the tracking reference its receipt (Receipt and Receipt-SHA256 trailers, the deploy's version id, the release tag), and its status follows the shipment states (shipped, returned on a refusal with its violation, reused). It is billable: the line is priced by the billing door in its own units (time and heat coins for the work, the catalogue's licence price where the tenant's licence names commercial use), recorded as a transaction against the tenant; no payment is ever taken automatically — a charge is the tenant's licence terms, settled by the tenant. Measured: code shipments / commits, pushes, deploys and releases, each with a tracking reference, exact pairs.

items.title: Hex and Glagolitic: binary native in the browser

arguments.text: Hex and Glagolitic: binary native in the browser. The user, 2026-10-27: "organise all around hex glagolytic so porting binary is native in browser". Every content address, block and sealed record is bytes; the browser now carries bytes natively — Uint8Array.prototype.toHex and Uint8Array.fromHex (ES2026, in current engines; Node 26 here has both) and TextEncoder/TextDecoder — so the port of binary is: bytes ⇄ hex by those natives, never a hand-written codec. Hex ⇄ Glagolitic: one nibble, one glyph. The tree's GLAGOLITIC table (src/quantum/i18n.ts: each letter with its numeric value) names the letters; sixteen of them, chosen by a stated rule from that table (the letters valued 1–9 and 10–60 in order, with one named glyph for 0), form a bijection with 0–F, so any hex — a UUID, a SHA-256, a whole sealed file — reads as Glagolitic text in the Unicode Glagolitic block (U+2C00–U+2C5F), searchable, copyable and rendered by the browser's own text stack. Theorem (decide over 16): the map is a bijection and its inverse round-trips every byte; the σ-reflection of a nibble (15 − n) maps to the glyph reflection, so the rosetta holds in both scripts. Organised around it: the crafted UUID, the content address in every block, Open Graph text and the gate's witnesses carry the Glagolitic form beside the hex; the core decodes either; the browser bundle uses only the natives (no polyfill where they exist, a measured fallback where they do not). Fonts: a Glagolitic-capable font stack with the fallback stated (a lead where a device lacks a glyph). Measured: addresses rendered both ways / addresses, round-trips exact / tried, exact pairs.

A task (qpu-google-call, qpu-raid-verify, the free-AI call to come) is queued by a call entry and answered by an entry found at uuidOf(request): for a predictable request (a public URL and the day) anyone can recompute that address, and call entries were readable by everyone. Every reader of an answer is keyed or server-side (askGoogle through the keyed MCP, qpuGoogle.ts through the Local API), so: (1) the kind call joins the operational group in ACCESS.groups, from which the Entries read is computed — a task's call and answer are read by their tenant and admins alone, while anyone may still create a call; (2) the answer's address is salted with the tenant's secret (HMAC-SHA-256 over the request under a key held by name, like the role MAC in roles.ts), so knowing a request is not knowing where its answer lives; (3) an answer stores no credential and no third party's embedded key — redacted by kind on write, the same redact as every record. Measured, exact: entries readable without a key whose kind is in the operational group (target 0, checked from the outside by the security scanner reading /api/entries anonymously), answers whose address a public request determines (target 0 once salted), answers holding a leak pattern (target 0).
